name: The Keeper
ins: The keeper calls his own by name, and the door will not answer him.
hint: The snake will chase you up the lane, but it will not step onto the exit. Let it follow you to the threshold and it will stop one cell short.

name: Separate Banks
ins: Two banks share one river, but never become one.
hint: A weight cannot climb back up, so choose its lower resting place carefully.

name: the honest stone
ins: The twin commits to the plate; it follows only where the floor allows, so choose a step it must refuse.
hint: Your twin repeats your every step. A bridge needs weight on its plate, so lead the twin into a pocket it cannot leave.

name: The Canonical Arch
ins: The canon feeds the echo; the echo never feeds the canon.
hint: Climb one tier at a time. The snake cannot follow even the first ledge.

name: The Queen of Venom
ins: The world moves only when you move.
hint: The queens converge behind you. Let the falling stones close their path, not yours.

name: The Unstamped Seal
ins: A hash by itself does not prove when.
hint: One crank remembers for both rivers. The gem's brittle detour has a lower way out.

name: out of phase
ins: Two patrols keep different clocks under one moon; the stone refuses odd strides and honors even ones, and a no left unexamined is a crossing skipped in silence.
hint: Each lizard advances one cell for every stride you take, each on its own beat; you cannot stand still, but stepping aside and back spends a beat. The spear judges only the parity of the stride you end on.

name: the mirror sentries
ins: Two keepers walk one road out of phase, each the other's mirror; the last door counts your steps and spares the even foot. An unexamined no is a silent skip.
hint: A keeper is most harmless just after it turns to walk away; count your steps onto the spear, for even feet are forgiven.

name: the scale: weight and shadow
ins: Two pans hang from one beam: set the stone and the door holds, but the shadow copies every step and the pit keeps what it is given.
hint: The bridge answers only to weight that stays. Climb the high lane and let the mirror trail you, for the hunter below counts every step you waste.

name: two swings, one fang
ins: It refused you on the odd beat, so you called the road closed; count the swing and the same fang is an open gate.
hint: Each lizard steps once after every step you take, swinging on a four beat pendulum. Enter a lane only while its rider is two squares away, and land on the fang only on an even count.

name: the charcoal weight
ins: Charcoal is free: draw the weight early, for the fang keeps strict hours and the mirror copies every line you make.
hint: The scale tips only while both pans are placed in time; your reflection is denied by stone, not by distance.

name: Below the Shrine
ins: Reach the shrine while the lizard patrols the lower lane.
hint: The fixed gem at [5,1] is on void, so it cannot be reached without changing the required base.

name: The Weight
ins: Some paths carry you only once.
hint: A weighted plate holds the bridge. Cracked stones offer a one-way detour with solid ground beyond.

name: stroke order
ins: Charcoal is free; stroke order is everything. The shadow waits in the dead end, the plate lights every bridge at once, and the critic can only cross where you have already crossed.
hint: Stop one step short of the bottom corner, then slip sideways while your shadow is denied by the void. One charcoal holds two bridges at once, even the gap caging the snake.

name: the garnet pocket
ins: The bridge east only holds while the block rests on the plate, and two crumbling cells guard an optional gem pocket past it.
hint: Collapse cells fall the moment you step off them, so only commit to crumbling ground when the far side offers a way home; a pocket sealed on three sides can still open upward.

name: the barbed junction
ins: Spear traps flank the crank junction and judge only where a step ends; wake the crank to throw the bridge, then cross on a count that never ends odd on barbed floor.
hint: A spear kills only if a move ENDS on it at an odd step count, so an even arrival is safe. A stepped crank latches every bridge for good, and a retracted bridge is void to everyone.

name: Two Watchers
ins: Reach the exit while two snakes close in.
hint: The exit is ground that neither snake can enter.

name: The Offered Weight
ins: An offering opens a shorter road, but no offering is required.
hint: Push the block sideways onto the plate to open the bridge. The original route remains open.

name: the closing door
ins: Drop into the lower pocket for the far gem, step across the crumbling tile, climb back up for the old gem, then descend to the bridge your twin holds.
hint: A collapse tile is a door that locks behind you: enter the pocket from above, never from the right. Your twin parks the moment your mirrored step is denied.

name: the mirror toll
ins: The reflection pays the toll it cannot refuse; burn the stairs behind you and cross on its shadow.
hint: A plate only works while something stands on it, and you have places to be. The twin copies each step only where the world allows; denied, it waits forever where it stands. Exactly one spot in this tomb can both hold it and hold the bridge.

name: the step it will not take
ins: An unexamined no is a silent skip: the serpent's refusals are the map, and the open lane is the lie.
hint: Serpents keep to their own height: they will not climb a step, will not stand on a crank, will not enter a door. Find where the floor rises, and touch the yes in passing without stopping.

name: the keeper's no
ins: It refuses this tile and never asked why. Its no is your quiet yes.
hint: Rises of one are doors the snake cannot open. A crank latches its bridge the moment you stand on it.

name: the odd middle
ins: The falsifier counted every landing on the middle stone and found them all odd, so waiting proves nothing; only the long arc retimes the crossing.
hint: A spear tastes only the step that lands on it: even counts stand, odd counts bleed, and no amount of loitering changes the count a cell will receive. The middle of the spear bar can never be stood on; climb where the count is even and let the one-way stone drop you past it.

name: the examined no
ins: An unexamined no is a silent skip; ask what the serpent cannot do before you accept what it forbids.
hint: The serpent cannot climb; one step up is a door it cannot open.

name: The Falsifier's Ledger
ins: The falsifier writes that waiting stills the blades; the ledger answers that every step turns the beat, and no waiting turns it back.
hint: Each move flips your beat, and pacing out and back flips it twice, so the beat you land on never changes no matter how you loiter. Blades only sleep on even beats, so read which stones can ever be safe before you commit, and recall the crumbling slab forgives no second visit.

name: Two Banks, One River
ins: Two banks, one river. What walks beside you walks across from you; the stone that stops you stops it too, and where the shadow rests, the river rests.
hint: Your twin copies every step one bank over, where the terrain mirrors yours, pillar for pillar. The walk that threads you past your pillar threads it past its own, and its last step can drop it on the plate. Once it stands there, finish moving east; a step down would bring it after you.

name: The Weight Remembers
ins: What falls stays fallen; the weight that settles on the plate keeps the bridge awake.
hint: A block slides down one height but never up, and once it settles it cannot be moved again. The pillar seals the west lane; only a push from the ledge top drops the weight true.

name: the far shore
ins: Two banks, one river. The plank between them wakes only while the still one stands on the far shore.
hint: Your reflection copies every step you take, even over the water. Walk it into the corner where the mirror has nothing left to touch, then go down and over while it stands.

name: The Weight Remembers
ins: The pillar has kept its weight since the river drank the road; lay your stone on the sunken plate and let the crossing remember you.
hint: The stone will not climb, but it will slide down one step; stand on the ledge above it, press it over the edge onto the sunken plate, and its resting weight holds the bridge true.

name: Cube Corridor
ins: It digests the straight path.
hint: push block down or detour via bridge

name: Mimic Plate
ins: the treasure is load-bearing.
hint: test the floor

name: The Blob That Doubles
ins: duplication is emphasis.
hint: This is a pre-split adaptation: blocks slide rather than duplicate. Collapse follows your footsteps; a parked copy can hold a plate.

name: The Splitting Blob: Aftermath
ins: emphasis is not redundancy.
hint: Fragments are preplaced, not spawned. One weighted plate powers the bridge, but all three fragments obstruct the passage.
